purpose: Portable project-semantics conformance corpus (PA5): executable evidence that the Nift CLI and the C++ project-aware Engine observe the same Nift project semantics, runnable against any implementation. Each case under cases/ is a fixture project + expected.json; run_conformance.py executes every case against the CLI and the Engine. nift-rs inherits this corpus later.

categories.parity: each page has a committed canonical golden (cases/<name>/expected/<page>.out/.deps/.reqs, generated from the reference CLI by gen_golden.py). The driver requires CLI output == golden AND Engine output == golden AND CLI output == Engine output; the same triple equality holds for dependency and requirement sets (golden vs CLI .info.json vs Engine result). This is an implementation-independent oracle, not merely two C++ paths agreeing.
categories.reject: both implementations reject the same invalid project or source state (CLI build fails; Engine render fails) AND the failure is for the intended semantic reason, validated by a stable diagnostic substring per REJECT_CLASSES in run_conformance.py (missing-source, unknown-config-key, duplicate-tracked-name, invalid-tracking-json, project-root-escape). Diagnostic prose is not a public contract; the semantic class is.
categories.engine-only: embedding contracts with no artificial CLI equivalent: Context value/title overlays, injected environment provider, unknown page, is_open()/open_error(). Executable evidence: tests/engine_project.cpp.
categories.lifecycle: C++ Engine serving contracts: atomic metadata-generation replacement via reload(), last-good retention on failed reload, zero-write serving. These are implementation contracts, NOT template-language semantics; nift-rs only inherits them if project-aware Rust adopts the same serving API. Executable evidence: tests/engine_reload.cpp.

pagination-contract: DECIDED (PA5): the project-aware Engine v1 renders a tracked page's primary pagination output. render("blog/") == the CLI's primary output public/blog/index.html (verified as a parity case). Explicit arbitrary pagination-page selection is NOT part of the current project-aware Engine contract and is deferred to future API design; no magic Context keys, no hastily invented render(page, number).
reject-taxonomy: The reject corpus distinguishes three classes of invalidity so nift-rs must reject for the intended reason, not merely fail somewhere: syntax-invalid project state (malformed-config, malformed-tracking: the project-state JSON itself cannot be parsed), semantically-invalid project state (bad-config unknown key, bad-tracking duplicate name: JSON parses but Nift rejects its semantics), and source/runtime invalidity (missing-source, path-escape).

cases.comprehensive: tracked-name lookup; index/trailing-slash geometry; content/template composition; metadata (title/name/content-path/output-path); @input; @json; contracts; tracked @pathto; concrete @pathto; 404 root-absolute geometry; pagination primary page; dependencies; requirements.
cases.schema: JSON schema validation and schema dependency recording.
cases.getenv: @getenv default process-environment semantics (driver sets the variable for both implementations).
cases.malformed-config: syntax-invalid project state: .nift/config.json is malformed JSON; both reject (invalid-config-json).
cases.malformed-tracking: syntax-invalid project state: valid config, .nift/tracked.json is malformed JSON; both reject (invalid-tracking-json).
cases.missing-source: source/runtime invalidity: tracked page whose content source is missing; both reject (missing-source).
cases.bad-config: semantically-invalid project state: unknown config key; both reject (unknown-config-key).
cases.bad-tracking: semantically-invalid project state: duplicate tracked name; both reject (duplicate-tracked-name).
cases.path-escape: source/runtime invalidity: @pathto escaping the project root; both reject (project-root-escape).
